Cc: novaprod-contracts@novaprod.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines and output/feedback carveouts

Rishi — thanks for sending the redline earlier this week. Our legal team has reviewed and we have two open items that we need to resolve before procurement can move forward: 1) the Order Form output assignment language — NovaProd needs clarity that outputs generated from our proprietary prompts and data are owned by us; 2) training/feedback license — we are not comfortable granting a perpetual training right over our customer content, but we are open to a timeboxed or escrowed approach.

Attached are our annotated redlines (PDF) and a suggested alternative paragraph for the training license. Can we schedule a quick sync tomorrow to walk through? Prefer 11–11:30 PT.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Senior Counsel, NovaProd
[Attachment: OrderForm_Draft_V2.pdf]

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@novaprod.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines and output/feedback carveouts

Ellen, thanks — received and appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers up front: we can tighten the Order Form language to call out customer-owned "customer-specific outputs" when generated from exclusively customer-provided prompts and data. For training/feedback, engineering and legal are resistant to permanently disabling learning from any customer interaction (it materially affects model quality and safety tuning), but I think a compromise is possible: a timebound feedback license (e.g., 12–24 months) plus an escrowed mechanism where NovaProd can opt out of training and request a verification artifact.

Laura — I’m looping you and Ben: can legal confirm whether a 12-month timebox + escrow verification is a workable compromise? Also, can we prepare a short language snippet for the Order Form that distinguishes: (a) customer inputs (owned by customer), (b) customer-specific outputs (assignment to customer when generated solely from customer inputs), and (c) general model improvements (retained by Redwood, with scrubbed telemetry)?

I can do the 11:00 PT sync tomorrow.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 10:05 AM rishi.malhotra@redwood.com wrote:
> Laura — I’m looping you and Ben: can legal confirm whether a 12-month timebox + escrow verification is a workable compromise?

Rishi — high level: yes, a limited-term feedback license is a common commercial compromise. A few guardrails we should include explicitly:
- Scope: license limited to non-identifiable, aggregated learning signals derived from metadata and anonymized telemetry (not raw customer content).
- Exclusions: never train on direct customer-provided files marked as "sensitive"; we should define a tagging flow for NovaProd to mark such uploads.
- Verification/escrow: propose a scope for the escrowed artifact — a redacted training snapshot or hash-based proof that no customer content was included post-opt-out. This has to be implementable by engineering; Ben, can your team scope the minimal verification artifact?

Ben — can you draft a one-paragraph engineering-safe verification option (2–3 sentences) we can propose to NovaProd during the call? I think saying "hash-based training manifest + redacted examples" might be feasible but want your take.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines and output/feedback carveouts — verification option

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 1:42 PM laura.bennett@redwood.com wrote:
> Ben — can you draft a one-paragraph engineering-safe verification option...

Quick draft we can use on the call or paste into the redline: 
"Verification artifact (engineering-safe): Redwood will produce a training manifest that lists anonymized dataset identifiers and per-batch hashes for any training run that incorporated customer feedback during the agreed license term. For any dataset identifier that NovaProd disputes, Redwood will provide a redacted sample (less than 1% of examples) with PII removed for independent review. The manifest and samples are intended solely for verification and will not include raw or unredacted customer data."

We should also be ready to offer an implementation timeline: we can support manifest generation within 30–45 days post-signoff for the initial pilot.

If that sounds good, I’ll paste into the Order Form supplement and we can test on tomorrow’s call.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
